name: Bag of Empty Ooze Containers
summary: In Ironforge, Laris Geardawdle supplies empty containers for his ooze research. The jars are meant to hold pristine slime specimens gathered in the field.

sections.title: Field Research Equipment
sections.body: Laris Geardawdle studies the strange biology of Azeroth's oozes. He found that slime creatures quickly take on the corruption around them, including tainted residues from Felwood. To study oozes in their natural state, he commissioned sturdy jars that can hold acidic specimens without harming them. The bag contains enough jars to collect clean slime in wild regions, especially Un'Goro Crater, where ancient glutinous oozes live free from demonic taint.

faq.q: What is inside the Bag of Empty Ooze Containers?
faq.answer: The bag holds ten Empty Pure Sample Jars, glass vessels made to store caustic ooze without damaging or contaminating the sample.

aliases: who gives bag of empty ooze containers
faq.answer: Laris Geardawdle, a gnome researcher working in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers, provided the containers. He studies how slimes adapt to their surroundings.

faq.q: What kind of oozes are these jars meant to collect?
aliases: what slime goes in the jars
faq.answer: The jars are meant for pure, uncorrupted ooze. Pristine slime can be collected from the glutinous oozes in Un'Goro Crater, unlike the blighted specimens in Felwood.

faq.q: Why does Laris need pure ooze samples?
faq.answer: Laris needs pure ooze samples to study how oozes absorb qualities from their surroundings. He can compare an uncorrupted specimen with polluted slimes from blighted regions.

angles.text: As a gnome, you can recognize the ingenuity in these durable, chemical-resistant jars, which let researchers carry dangerous, corrosive wildlife samples safely.
As an Alliance adventurer, you can help Laris Geardawdle with his ecological research from Ironforge by bringing back field samples from untamed places like Un'Goro Crater.
